results.name: Double Kettlebell Sled Push
instructions: Place two kettlebells on the sled and grip the sled handles.
Lean into the sled at about 45 degrees with your arms extended.
Drive forward with powerful steps through the balls of your feet.
Keep pushing for the set distance.
tips: Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Drive your knees forward.
results.description: Double Kettlebell Sled Push is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Hamstrings, Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Swing
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell vertically with both hands between your legs, keeping your arms extended.
Push your hips backward and bend your knees as you swing the dumbbell between your legs while maintaining a straight back.
Drive your hips forward and straighten your legs to swing the dumbbell upward until your arms reach approximately shoulder height.
Allow the dumbbell to descend with control, hinge your hips backward as it passes between your legs, and continue for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Generate the upward movement by driving your hips forward rather than lifting primarily with your arms.
Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding your back during the downward swing.
Control the dumbbell as it travels between your legs instead of allowing it to pull you forward.
Inhale as the dumbbell swings downward and exhale as you drive your hips forward.
results.description: Dumbbell Swing is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Lower Back, Core.

results.name: Front Lever Raise to Hold
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, your arms straight, and your legs together.
Engage your core and raise your legs and torso together until your body is parallel to the floor.
Keep your arms and legs straight as you hold the horizontal position.
Slowly lower your body back to the hanging position, then repeat.
tips: Keep your body straight from your shoulders to your feet.
Keep your elbows fully extended throughout the movement.
Avoid swinging or using momentum.
Exhale as you raise your body and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Front Lever Raise to Hold is an advanced single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Front Lever Raise
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, your arms straight, and your legs together.
Engage your core and raise your legs and torso together while keeping your body straight.
Continue lifting past horizontal until your feet rise above the bar.
Lower your body with control until you return to the hanging position, then repeat.
tips: Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
Keep your core engaged during the lowering phase.
Avoid swinging or using momentum.
Exhale as you raise your body and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Front Lever Raise is an advanced single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Gorilla Walk
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width and squat down until you can place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Place your hands on the floor and shift your weight onto them.
Hop or step your feet forward to land outside your hands.
Repeat, moving forward in a low, gorilla-like stance.
tips: Keep your hips low and your back flat.
Land softly.
results.description: Gorilla Walk is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Core, Hamstrings.

results.name: Gym Elliptical Machine Fast Speed
instructions: Step on the elliptical machine and place your feet securely on the pedals. Grip the handles with both hands for stability.
Begin moving your legs in a smooth, elliptical motion, coordinating with the handles as they move back and forth. Start at a moderate pace to get comfortable with the movement.
Gradually increase your speed to a fast pace, maintaining a smooth and controlled motion with both your legs and arms.
Continue pedaling and moving the handles at a fast pace for the desired duration.
tips: Breathe steadily and deeply to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Focus on using both your legs and arms to distribute the effort evenly and prevent early fatigue.
Adjust the resistance level if needed to provide a challenging but manageable workout.
results.description: Gym Elliptical Machine Fast Speed is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with an elliptical machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Gym Rowing Machine Fast Speed
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet securely strapped into the footrests, knees bent, and hands grasping the handle with an overhand grip.
Push through your legs to extend your knees and drive your body backward, keeping your arms straight until your legs are almost fully extended.
Just before your legs are fully extended, pull the handle towards your lower chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Reverse the motion by extending your arms forward first, then bending your knees to return to the starting position. Repeat the motion at a fast pace for the desired duration.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your spine throughout the exercise.
Use a moderate resistance level to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Exhale as you pull, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Gym Rowing Machine Fast Speed is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a rowing machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Shoulders, Arms.

Just before your legs are fully extended, pull the handle towards your lower chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Reverse the motion by extending your arms forward first, then bending your knees to return to starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or time.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your spine throughout the exercise.
Use a moderate resistance level to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Exhale as you pull, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Gym Rowing Machine Normal Speed is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a rowing machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Shoulders, Arms.
